audit_findings.title: Mixed anchor and bridge dates may double-count interim earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $31.518 million, or $1.09 per share and 1.57% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: A full-year 2026 operating cash flow starting from the FY2025 anchor could overlap with first-half 2026 cash already included in the June 30 bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Our cash and cash equivalents at December 31, 2025 increased to $371.1 million from $278.0 million at December 31, 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The date mismatch is demonstrated, but double-counting is not established because the forecast timing convention is unspecified. Cash increased from $371.124 million to $402.642 million during the first half, bounding the observable post-2025 cash added to the bridge at $31.518 million. Even removing that entire increment would reduce value by only $1.09 per share, versus the $37.31 gap between the $116.69 price and $79.38 bull value, so it cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Document the first forecast cash-flow date and discount periods. If the DCF includes January-June 2026, remove $31.518 million from the bridge or replace 2026 with a June 30 stub and rerun.

audit_findings.title: A perpetual terminal value may outlive economically available reserves
audit_findings.magnitude: Terminal value represents a computed $548.1 million to $1,003.4 million across scenarios; the reserve-related reduction is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Finite reserve lives and replacement or conversion expenditures affect terminal growth, terminal reinvestment, and the duration of operating owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: Based on the projected level of production and recovery rates, the Company estimates that these reserves are sufficient to sustain its limestone operations for approximately 17 years.
audit_findings.explanation: The 17-year life applies to Batesville, while the connected Love Hollow quarry reports more than 80 years of reserves, Texas approximately 70 years, St. Clair approximately 37 years, and total disclosed material-property reserves are 223.150 million tons. The record therefore does not demonstrate that consolidated operations terminate shortly after year ten. Nevertheless, because terminal value supplies 47.7%-53.2% of operating PV and property-level earnings and replacement costs are unavailable, the possible effect could be important but materiality cannot presently be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain property-level production, owner earnings, reserve depletion, Love Hollow substitution capacity, permits, and reserve-conversion or replacement costs; rerun using property-specific finite lives and explicit terminal reinvestment.

audit_findings.title: Gross cash may include funds already committed to expansion
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.5 million, or $0.09 per share and 0.12% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Unfunded binding capital commitments would reduce surplus cash unless already included in forecast reinvestment.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025, the Company had $18,599 for open equipment and construction services contracts.
audit_findings.explanation: The December 2025 commitment of $18.599 million is superseded for bridge purposes by the June 2026 filing: only $2.5 million of Texas-kiln open purchase orders remained and no other material open-order commitments existed. Whether that amount is already forecast is unresolved, but deducting all of it changes value by only about $0.09 per share and cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether the remaining $2.5 million is included in projected capital spending; if not, deduct it once from the June cash bridge.

audit_findings.title: Normalized earnings may still depend on unusually strong demand and pricing
audit_findings.mechanism: Temporary volumes, prices, or margins could lower normalized owner earnings and make the 6% and 9% growth paths unattainable.
audit_findings.evidence: Specifically, demand from our utility customers has decreased due to the recent trend in the United States towards reducing reliance on coal-fired utility plants, and current areas of active growth, such as data center construction, may not continue.
audit_findings.explanation: This is presently a forward-looking demand risk rather than a demonstrated normalization error. First-half 2026 revenue increased 2.3%, operating profit increased 1.1%, and second-quarter revenue increased 8.3%; management also expected data-center projects to continue supporting construction demand. Those results do not establish a reversal, but the filings do not quantify data-center-related volumes or their margins, so the durability of assumed growth remains unmeasurable.
audit_findings.action: Track data-center volumes, customer mix, realized pricing, utilization, and margins separately; rerun normalized owner earnings and the growth cases if post-year-end results show sustained demand or margin erosion.

audit_findings.title: Asset-retirement principal may be an unmodeled claim ahead of equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.401 million, or $0.05 per share and 0.07% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: ARO settlement cash must appear in forecast owner earnings or be deducted as a liability in the equity bridge to avoid omission.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company’s AROs of $1,401 and $1,484 as of December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively, are included in Other liabilities and Accrued expenses on the Company’s Consolidated Balance Sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The record does not establish whether settlement cash flows are already captured, so the modeling omission remains possible. However, the filed December 2025 ARO was only $1.401 million, including estimated spending of approximately $0.1 million annually through 2030. Deducting the entire recorded obligation would reduce value by about $0.05 per share and cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 30, 2026 ARO rollforward and confirm forecast settlement cash flows; if absent, deduct the updated recorded ARO once from the bridge.
